reasons: We are the customer/buyer (IBM); every audit, inspection and verification right in the cited text (p0163-p0164 process audits at MSL's Work Centers, p1443 audit/inspection of MSL's and its Subsidiaries' books, records and facilities on 45 days' notice by an independent CPA) runs in our favour against the supplier, so nothing binds us on frequency, notice, cost or system access.
p0317 (Records) is a mutual record-retention obligation only and confers no audit or inspection right over our premises, records or systems, so it creates no exposure under this rule.

No remote or direct access to our systems is granted anywhere in the cited text, so the walk-away trigger is not implicated; classifying this as compliant with no redline and no comment is correct for a clause that benefits our party.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is not probative here: the frequency cap is a protection we would need only if the audit right ran against us, and the redline correctly leaves the counterparty-facing audit rights untouched.
